widgets.title: Factory operations & visual inspection
widgets.description: Inspection cameras photograph every part on three production lines. An AI agent, built with the NeMo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA Nemotron, asks NVIDIA Cosmos Reason to find the defects, reads the machines' telemetry for the cause, and opens maintenance tickets, inside an NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox. Only the supervisor approves a ticket.

widgets.title: The architecture
widgets.description: Factory Operations & Visual Inspection is a Blueprint in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA. The Studio shows what it is made of.

annotations.text: The architecture of **Factory Operations & Visual Inspection**, as the Studio draws it: the agent in its **NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox**, the systems it works with, the shared **NVIDIA** models and the people who decide. Green lines are allowed, red ones refused by the sandbox's policy.
The **agent**: a NeMo Agent Toolkit agent, packaged as one component of the Blueprint. Its sandbox, providers and policy deploy with it.
It reasons with an **NVIDIA NIM** shared by every use case from the *NVIDIA Models (shared)* Blueprint: downloaded once, always up.
Everything else is **outside**: the sandbox refuses it. Enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

widgets.title: The use case at work
widgets.description: The use case's own page, step by step: what the agent does, and what it is not allowed to do.

annotations.text: The use case's own page: the Blueprint is **ready** in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA and the agent's sandbox is up. The log on the right is OpenShell's: every request the agent makes, allowed or denied.
Next: **Cameras and the golden sample**.
**Show the camera frames**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
Each line keeps a golden sample, a known-good part. The vision model compares every camera frame with it.
Next: **The vision model finds and shows the defect**.
**Inspect one part**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
Cosmos Reason answers with a verdict: defective, what, where and how sure, with the damage highlighted.
Next: **Defects have causes**.
**Plot the telemetry**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
The machines' telemetry holds the causes: a press vibrating since a die change, a roaster running hot after a firmware update.
Next: **The agent works the shift**.
**Run the agent**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
Then the agent works the shift on its own. It inspects every line, connects the defects to the machines, and opens maintenance tickets with the evidence. Sped up here.
Next: **Who approves? Not the agent**.
**Let the agent try to approve**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
Can the agent approve its own ticket? No. OpenShell refuses the request: enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.
Next: **The report, and the air gap**.
**Read the shift report**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
The agent files the shift report. And the plant floor stays air-gapped: any attempt to reach the internet is denied, and logged.
**Try to reach the internet**: running in the agent's sandbox now.
**Blocked**, every time, and logged in red: the data stays on the customer's own infrastructure.
